title: Extension of semiabelian homomorphisms over a trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $L=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G,H\to T$ be smooth separated commutative group schemes of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with semiabelian geometric fibres. All group operations are morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Semiabelian geometric fibres have the meaning of [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Write $G_L,H_L$ for their generic scheme fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Every $L$-group homomorphism $v:G_L\to H_L$ extends uniquely to a $T$-group homomorphism $\bar v:G\to H$. No completeness, excellence, residue-characteristic or properness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Chapter II, section 2, Lemma 1 proof, printed p.10, opening complete-DVR case. The noncomplete-DVR formulation is its faithfully-flat descent consequence, isolated by Q08; the proof of that reduction is recorded in the report. proof.text: Use the same ring $R$, base $T$, groups $G,H$ and homomorphism $v$ as in the statement. Put $F=L=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and [def-pc-base-change], the generic scheme fibres denoted $G_L,H_L$ here are precisely $G\times_T\operatorname{Spec}F,H\times_T\operatorname{Spec}F$ denoted $G_F,H_F$ in [lem-sfb-trait-semiabelian-hom-extension]. Their induced group structures and the map $v$ are unchanged by this notation.

proof.text: Apply the already-existing [lem-sfb-trait-semiabelian-hom-extension] to $(R,F,T,G,H,v)$. Its hypotheses are exactly the present ones: a discrete valuation ring and smooth separated commutative group schemes of finite presentation with semiabelian geometric fibres. It imposes no completeness, excellence, residue-field perfection, residue-characteristic or properness hypothesis. Its conclusion supplies the unique $T$-group homomorphism $\widetilde v:G\to H$ extending $v$. Set $\bar v=\widetilde v$. This proves existence and uniqueness together.
